title: A flat subgroup containing an identity neighbourhood is open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $H,G$ be group objects in schemes over $S$, with identity sections $e_H,e_G$, multiplication and inverse. Let $i:H\hookrightarrow G$ be an $S$-group homomorphism which is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $H\to S$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose there is an open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow G$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and morphisms $e_V:S\to V$ and $b:V\to H$ over $S$ such that $ve_V=e_G$ and $ib=v$. Then $i$ is an open immersion. Neither $H\to S$ nor $G\to S$ is assumed smooth, and no connectedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), final proof, printed p.289, translation from a neighbourhood of the identity. Agent general tool formulation: multiplication of H with V is flat and locally finitely presented, hence open, and its open image contains H; fpqc local exactness of a closed ideal identifies H with that open image. Online source read; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme theorem.

proof.text: Put $P=H\times_SG$ and $D=H\times_SV$. The group laws define inverse $S$-automorphisms of $P$, $a(h,g)=(h,i(h)g)$ and $a^{-1}(h,g)=(h,i(h)^{-1}g)$: their composites are the identity by associativity and the inverse law. These formulas mean morphisms formed from the two projections and the group operations, so apply over every test scheme. The morphism $j=1_H\times v:D\to P$ is a base change of $v$, hence an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Consequently $k=a\circ j$ is an open immersion: the automorphism carries the open subscheme identified by $j$ to its isomorphic open subscheme. Define $q=\operatorname{pr}_G\circ k:D\to G$, so $q(h,t)=i(h)v(t)$.

source.place: Agent translation construction; Schemes Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), open-immersion case.

proof.text: The projection $p=\operatorname{pr}_G:P\to G$ is the base change of $H\to S$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The open immersion $k$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-flat-compose] and [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] to $D\xrightarrow{k}P\xrightarrow{p}G$. Thus $q$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. No flatness of $G\to S$ is used.

By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $U=q(|D|)$ is open in $|G|$. There is a morphism $r:D\to H$, $r(h,t)=h\,b(t)$, with $i\circ r=q$, because $i$ respects multiplication and $i\circ b=v$. Conversely define $s:H\to D$ by $s(h)=(h,e_V(p_H(h)))$, where $p_H:H\to S$ is the structure map. Since $v\circ e_V=e_G$, the identity law gives $q\circ s=i$. The two factorizations imply $q(|D|)\subseteq i(|H|)$ and $i(|H|)\subseteq q(|D|)$ respectively. Hence $U=i(|H|)$. The closed immersion $i$ is therefore a homeomorphism of $|H|$ onto the open subspace $U$, by [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open); agent argument using the specified multiplication and identity morphisms.

proof.text: Fix $h\in H$ and put $u=i(h)$. Choose $z\in D$ with $q(z)=u$, which exists by Step 3 (one may take $z=s(h)$). Since $i\circ r=q$ and $i$ is injective on points, $r(z)=h$. The stalk map $q_z^\sharp:\mathcal O_{G,u}\to\mathcal O_{D,z}$ is a flat local ring homomorphism by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. It is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat], and injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with $N=\mathcal O_{G,u}$, identifying $N\otimes_N\mathcal O_{D,z}$ with $\mathcal O_{D,z}$ by $a\otimes c\mapsto q_z^\sharp(a)c$. Functoriality of germs gives $q_z^\sharp=r_z^\sharp\circ i_h^\sharp$, so $i_h^\sharp$ is injective. It is also surjective: the affine quotient description of [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies it locally with $A_{\mathfrak p}\to(A/I)_{\mathfrak p/I}$, whose elements are the images of fractions in $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus $i_h^\sharp$ is an isomorphism for every $h$.

source.place: Tags 00HR (lemma-local-flat-ff) and 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective); affine quotient clause of Morphisms Tag 01QO.

proof.text: Use the homeomorphism $|H|\simeq U$ from Step 3 to regard $\mathcal O_H$ as a sheaf on $U$. The structure map is then a morphism of sheaves of rings $\mathcal O_G|_U\to\mathcal O_H$ whose stalk maps are exactly the isomorphisms of Step 4: the corresponding neighbourhoods are identified by this homeomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks] to the underlying sheaves of sets on $U$. The structure map is bijective on sections over every open. The inverses preserve addition, multiplication and the unit because the forward section maps are bijective ring homomorphisms; the inverses commute with restrictions by inverting the naturality squares. Thus it is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. Together with Step 3, [def-weil-open-immersion] proves that $i$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 007T (lemma-points-exactness), part (3); definition of open immersion, Schemes Tags 01HE and 01IO.
